title: SPARC: Evidence-guided adaptive model composition for materials discovery
abstract: arXiv:2611.19050v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Closed-loop experimentation requires more than selecting the next experiment. It must also determine which existing measurements and model-derived relationships are sufficiently supported to influence that decision. Here we introduce SPARC (Sparse Predictive Aggregation of Regression Components), a framework that continually revises this support as experimental evidence accumulates. Competing model families are evaluated through out-of-fold predictions, so that each model is tested on observations not used in its corresponding fit. Sparse posterior composition assigns model influence according to predictive contributions supported by the out-of-fold evidence, retaining complementary contributions from several model families. Candidate-dependent predictive dispersion and residual variability define trust, which modulates exploration alongside the predicted response. translated_title: SPARC：面向材料发现的证据引导自适应模型组合
translated_abstract: 闭环实验不仅需要选择下一个实验，还必须确定哪些现有测量结果和模型推导的关系获得了足够充分的支持，从而能够影响该决策。本文提出了SPARC（回归组件的稀疏预测聚合，Sparse Predictive Aggregation of Regression Components），这是一个随着实验证据积累而不断修正上述支持程度的框架。相互竞争的模型族通过折外预测进行评估，使每个模型在其对应拟合中未使用的观测数据上接受检验。稀疏后验组合根据折外证据所支持的预测贡献来分配各模型的影响力，同时保留来自多个模型族的互补贡献。候选依赖的预测离散度和残差变异性共同定义了信任度，该信任度与预测响应一起调节探索过程。独立的诊断机制还会对现有测量结果进行优先级排序，以便进行前瞻性的重新评估。
tldr: SPARC是一个面向材料发现闭环实验的自适应模型组合框架，通过折外预测评估竞争模型族、以稀疏后验聚合分配模型权重，并利用预测离散度与残差变异性定义信任度来调节探索策略。
en_tdlr: SPARC is an evidence-guided adaptive model composition framework for closed-loop materials discovery that evaluates competing model families via out-of-fold predictions, assigns sparse posterior weights based on evidence-supported contributions, and defines trust through predictive dispersion and residual variability to modulate exploration.
